P1.evidence: Setter suffix KFS indicates pre-qualification but no application or setter notes were read back. No four-part frame was set and no frame agreement sought — the rep went straight from small talk to 'we have a limited amount of time. Should we hop into it?'. The opening question was a variant rather than the scripted one: 'where else did you come across Trevor and Kettlebell Body?' followed by 'What specifically resonated and stood out to you?'

P2.evidence: Baseline was almost entirely skipped. No age, height or weight. Work was asked ('What do you do for work') but not whether it is desk-bound. Health conditions were never asked; the injury history and the ongoing physical therapy were volunteered by the prospect while answering a root-cause question, which scores as a miss. Only the training week was properly elicited: 'What does your routine look like now? Say Monday to Sunday?'. Diet, sleep and energy were never raised at any point.

P3.evidence: Strong future-pacing: 'If a genie could essentially click their fingers, say 2027, May the 1st. How do you want to operate in your body?' pulled out the suits, the marathon times and the confidence gap. The bridge past the physical ran well — 'is there anything that is internally driving you to be your best self?' — and the rep landed identity: 'is that kind of where your identity is formed from... you carry yourself as elite in other areas'. But the ripple-effect questions were never asked: no 'when you're moving better, what does that do for you' and, critically, no 'who else does that impact' — family, marriage and legacy were never touched in a 40-minute call. The reflect-back was delivered as a statement without confirmation: 'It's about longevity for you. It's about pushing your limits as a human being.'

P4.evidence: The strongest phase of the call. 'So what have you been trying on your own to get there thus far?' then 'when you say you've tried kettlebells, like how long, when?' and 'is this something you still do?'. Root cause was pushed hard — 'why haven't you been able to lose body fat, get yourself into the shape that you want... over the last six or seven years? Why hasn't that happened yet?' — and the rep ran the self-sufficiency challenge in the scripted spirit: 'what's the rationale for you in terms of getting outside help with this, as opposed to just following YouTube, ChatGPT?'. The prospect named the gap himself: 'I think it's accountability, just an accountability partner.'

P5.evidence: The Consequence Frame was not run at all. No two-year cost-of-inaction question, no 'are you willing to settle for that', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep moved directly from root cause to 'I'm pretty confident that we can help you... Brian, you have a pen, paper, laptop, iPad?' and into the three pillars. With no cost of inaction established, price arrived unbuffered.

P6.evidence: A confidence gauge was run, but after the presentation rather than before it, which inverts the script's intent: '10 out of 10 is I feel like these guys could help me, I trust Trevor, and one is I'm not sure if I need this. Where would you put this?' — answer 8 or 9. The follow-up 'Why are we not here at the 12?' is a weak stand-in for 'is there any reason you wouldn't go all in'. It surfaced the blocker — 'there's value as well... pricing and value come into play' — and the rep did not return to Phase 5. He presented price into a stated 8-or-9 with an unresolved value caveat.

P11.evidence: No agreement was reached, so payment, the Trevor onboarding call, the agreement email and the Skool/questionnaire steps were all unreachable. The prospect rejected the coaching offer on price and deferred on the community product.

objection_plays.detail: Price resistance landed twice — 'that's way out of my expectation' at 00:29:06 and 'that's out of my range' at 00:38:16 — and not one move of the open-wallet play ran. No isolation ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%'), no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no offer to break it up, no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture questions. The rep's response to the first was 'Sure. All good, man. All good'; his response to the second was to re-present the $200/mo community product. This is the single largest process failure on the call.

'I'm going to, I guess, think about it' at 00:32:39 and 'I want to think about it a little more' at 00:39:11. The rep ran exactly one scripted move — 'when you say you want to think about it, just so I'm on the same page, what do you need to go over before making that decision?' — and stopped there. Missing: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'when do you make a different decision', and the final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'.

A textbook timing trigger: 'I'm three weeks out from my next marathon... three weeks out from a marathon, I'm not doing anything different.' No move ran. The rep did not ask 'when does it actually become the right time', did not point out that the prospect has three marathons booked this year so the window never opens, and did not use 'what if all you had to do was show up'. Instead he proposed the deferral himself: 'would it make sense to potentially revisit this and have myself message you around that three-week mark?'

SCRIPT GAP — remote-versus-in-person. The prospect's stated blocker was modality, not money: 'I do think there is a different dynamic when it's in-person versus remote', backed by a specific failed experience — 'I had a remote coach during the pandemic, it wasn't the same... at that time it was better than nothing'. There is no play for this. The rep reverse-questioned ('so then why go the virtual route?') and accepted the answer, never using the weekly film-and-review feedback loop he had already described as the direct answer to it. This is a gap in the playbook, not a rep failure.

SCRIPT GAP — endurance-sport periodisation. The prospect could not evaluate the offer because nobody could tell him how loaded kettlebell work integrates with a marathon taper and a three-race season. No scripted path exists for a prospect whose primary sport dictates their training calendar.

notes: Phase 4 was genuinely good — the rep got the prospect to name accountability as his own gap, unprompted. Everything after it fell over: the Consequence Frame was skipped entirely, so when price landed there was no cost of inaction to weigh it against, and the money objection was answered with a downsell inside sixty seconds rather than with any part of Objection C. Coach the sequence 'isolate, then explore, then downsell only if the isolation fails' — the rep skipped straight to step three, twice.
